metadata.Name: HellaSwag
metadata.Description: A challenge dataset for commonsense natural language inference. It contains 70k multiple-choice questions that are trivial for humans (>95% accuracy) but difficult for state-of-the-art models. It was created using Adversarial Filtering to generate challenging wrong answers from WikiHow and ActivityNet Captions.
metadata.Paper Title: HellaSwag: Can a Machine Really Finish Your Sentence?
metadata.Venue Title: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Affiliations: Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering, University of Washington
metadata.Abstract: Recent work by Zellers et al. (2018) introduced a new task of commonsense natural language inference : given an event description such as 'A woman sits at a piano,' a machine must select the most likely followup: 'She sets her fingers on the keys.' With the introduction of BERT (Devlin et al., 2018), near human-level performance was reached. Does this mean that machines can perform human level commonsense inference?nnIn this paper, we show that commonsense inference still proves di GLYPH<14> cult for even stateof-the-art models, by presenting HellaSwag , a new challenge dataset. Though its questions are trivial for humans ( ¡ 95% accuracy), state-of-the-art models struggle ( GLYPH<160> 48%). We achieve this via Adversarial Filtering (AF), a data collection paradigm wherein a series of discriminators iteratively select an adversarial set of machine-generated wrong answers. AF proves to be surprisingly robust. The key insight is to scale up the length and complexity of the dataset examples towards a critical 'Goldilocks' zone wherein generated text is ridiculous to humans, yet often misclassified by state-of-the-art models.nnOur construction of HellaSwag , and its resulting di GLYPH<14> culty, sheds light on the inner workings of deep pretrained models. More broadly, it suggests a new path forward for NLP research, in which benchmarks co-evolve with the evolving state-of-the-art in an adversarial way, so as to present ever-harder challenges.
